note: Tables Supabase's own services write while an application runs. Each entry is bookkeeping that carries no application effect. Tables that do carry one stay off the list on purpose, so they read as unlisted (an absence cannot pass) until a profile declares and observes them or lists them itself: auth.users, auth.identities, auth.one_time_tokens and auth.mfa_factors (accounts, logins sent, factors); storage.objects and storage.buckets (files); realtime.messages (broadcasts sent to clients); cron.job (scheduled jobs); net.http_request_queue (outbound requests pg_net sends); vault and pgsodium (secrets). pg_net creates its request queue unlogged, so pg-wal cannot read it: while it exists every pg-wal window reads table-not-in-wal until the profile lists it, which a profile should do only once those requests are observed on the wire (an egress recorder under a confined run). Drawn from the schemas those services create; not yet checked against a live Supabase stack, so read a first run's other-table record before relying on it.
